title: Protein and amino acid requirements in human nutrition
journal: World Health Organization Technical Report Series, No. 935
funder: Joint WHO/FAO/UNU Expert Consultation held at WHO headquarters, Geneva, 9-16 April 2002; the report states no other source of funding.
result: Nutritionally indispensable amino acids: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan and valine; conditionally indispensable: e.g. cysteine, tyrosine, taurine, glycine, arginine, glutamine and proline. Adult average protein requirement 0.66 g/kg per day; safe level 0.83 g/kg per day for protein with a protein digestibility-corrected amino acid score of 1.0, expected to meet the needs of 97.5% of healthy adults. Mean adult indispensable amino acid requirements (mg/kg per day): histidine 10, isoleucine 20, leucine 39, lysine 30, methionine plus cysteine 15, phenylalanine plus tyrosine 25, threonine 15, tryptophan 4, valine 26.
